in_text_mentions: On presentation, the patient appeared nontoxic and was afebrile. His heart rate was 104 beats/min, while all other vital signs were within normal limits. Physical examination demonstrated bilateral, symmetrical, sharply demarcated erythema, warmth, and edema involving the malar regions and nasal bridge, with extension toward the periorbital areas (Figure 1). There was no fluctuance, purulent drainage, crepitus, or skin necrosis. The remainder of the physical examination was otherwise unremarkable.

source_variant.figure_caption: Hemorrhagic Bullous Lesion in Advanced Bullous Erysipelas A large, tense, hemorrhagic bulla located on the anterior aspect of the left lower leg, surrounded by extensive erythema, violaceous discoloration, and areas of skin necrosis. The lesion developed progressively following inadequate initial antibiotic treatment and was initially mistaken for necrotizing fasciitis before a final diagnosis of bullous erysipelas was made.
